intro: Iraq is shaped by two great rivers, the Tigris and the Euphrates, which flow from Turkey to the Gulf.

chapters.title: Two rivers
text: Most Iraqis live along the rivers, which have watered farms for thousands of years. They join near Basra to form the Shatt al-Arab, which flows into the Gulf.
Dams upstream in Turkey and Iran, and drought, have reduced the rivers' flow.

chapters.title: Mountains, desert and marshes
text: The north-east is mountainous Kurdistan. The west is desert reaching into Syria, Jordan and Saudi Arabia. In the south, the Mesopotamian Marshes are home to the Marsh Arabs, who build houses from reeds; Saddam drained much of them in the 1990s, but they have partly recovered.

chapters.title: Heat
text: Summers are extremely hot: Basra often passes 50 °C. Dust storms are common.
